transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Evan Morris (Redwood AE), Samira Kahn (Redwood SE), Jules Park (Redwood CSM), Dr. Leo Park (Head of IT - Nightingale), Maya Chen (Security Engineer), Ravi Patel (CTO)

Summary: quick security posture intake — customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PHI-adjacent inference workloads. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO proof, customer-managed KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC mapping to AD groups, audit log retention/export, EU data residency and air-gap requirement for one regulated program.

Topics:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001)
- SSO (Okta) and SCIM flows, user provisioning
- KMS options: Redwood-managed vs customer-managed AWS KMS vs HSM
- Audit logs and retention (90 days vs 1 year vs 7 years for regulated studies)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for latency/cost/control
- Pilot/benchmark next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan: hey everyone, thanks for taking time. quick intro from our side — im evan, i'm the AE on the account, samira is our solutions eng and will run the deep bits.
[00:08] Ravi: hey, ravi here. we uh we may jump around a bit, we have a handful of compliance folks but for today maya and leo are primary.
[00:16] Maya: hi all, thanks. main thing: we process PHI-adjacent data, looking for a plan that keeps logs and keys under our control where needed.
[00:25] Samira: ok great, that's helpful. just to calibrate, can you tell us which workload you're most worried about? latency sensitive? batch only?
[00:34] Dr. Park: the primary workload is clinical triage assistant — real-time-ish, so latency matters, but also we have consented study datasets that require stricter residency and longer retention.
[00:46] Evan: makes sense. so two axes: low-latency hosted path vs private/dedicated for control. before we dig into KMS and SSO, wanted to confirm compliance checklist: SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence are must-haves?
[00:58] Maya: yes. plus our legal team will want audit log exports for any regulated study for up to 7 years — that's non-negotiable.
[01:07] Jules: to flag — our audit log retention product supports configurable windows; we can export in standard JSON/CSV and ship to S3 or your SIEM. i'll add samples after the call.
[01:19] Maya: cool, format matters. also, we need to know if keys can be customer-managed HSM, not only cloud KMS.
[01:27] Samira: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and there is a pathway for HSM integration in Private deployments — the on-prem package can front a customer HSM. caveat: hosted with CMK has different threat model than air-gapped HSM.
[01:46] Dr. Park: can you outline what changes for us if we pick Dedicated vs Private? especially around key custody and audit logs.
[01:55] Samira: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our managed infra; you can bring your own CMK for encryption-at-rest and we can route audit logs to your S3. but the control plane is still Redwood-hosted, so admin audit trails for the control plane remain with us (we provide role-based access for your admins). Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control — control plane runs in your environment, keys can remain behind your HSM, and we can disable outbound telemetry if required. tradeoffs: Private has longer onboarding and higher ops burden, Dedicated is faster to stand up and typically cheaper than building in-house.
[02:28] Ravi: and SOC2? if we go Private, do you still provide SOC2 assurances?
[02:33] Evan: good question. SOC2 covers Redwood's hosted operations; for Private deployments you get a set of artifacts and we run a formal attestation for components we operate (if under contract). but because the control plane is customer-run, the SOC2 scope in your vendor assessment will differ — we'll give guidance and docs.
[02:47] Maya: ok. next — SSO. we use Okta, SCIM provisioning, and want RBAC mapped to AD groups. is that supported?
[02:55] Samira: yes — SAML SSO with Okta is supported, and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC can sync from SCIM groups; we map to our role model (viewer/editor/operator/admin). you'll be able to lock down per-route token permissions too. small note: for Private we can wire direct LDAP/AD integration for on-premise mapping if you prefer.
[03:19] Dr. Park: any latency cost for SSO lookups? like on token exchange?
[03:24] Samira: negligible; SSO is an auth flow and we issue short-lived tokens — actual inference path doesn't consult IdP per request. so no runtime latency impact.
[03:34] Maya: about audit logs — we need to record per-token usage, model version, prompt hash, and output checksums for reproducibility. do you capture those?
[03:44] Jules: yes. our logs capture token counts, model id, request metadata (route, model version, user id if present), and we can include a prompt fingerprint. we redact PII by default in hosted but can configure retention and redaction behavior per contract.
[03:58] Maya: redaction is ok but we need an unredacted copy for regulated study vaults — can you do that?
[04:05] Samira: in Dedicated and Private deployments we can arrange for privileged logging to be forwarded to your secure S3/HSM with access controls; for Hosted there's a strict isolation and we typically don't provide unredacted copies unless under customer-managed key agreements.
[04:19] Dr. Park: ok that's helpful. could you also outline egress and data residency? our EU study requires compute + storage in eu-west-1.
[04:28] Evan: we have regional hosting and can pin workloads to eu-west-1; Dedicated pools can be provisioned in EU regions. Private on-prem can be deployed in your datacenter. again, we'd script routing to keep data in-region.
[04:37] Ravi: pricing note — what's the delta for Dedicated with CMK vs Hosted? we need rough ballpark for finance.
[04:44] Evan: quickly: hosted is lowest capex and per-token price. Dedicated adds reserved capacity cost (monthly commitment) and a small premium for CMK routing. Private has a higher fixed onboarding fee and ongoing support license. i'll follow up with a pricing sheet.
[04:58] Maya: security questionnaires — we'll run your answers through third-party legal. do you have an SSP/SSO/QSA pack?
[05:05] Evan: yes, we have an SSP and a security questionnaire packet; i'll attach the latest SSP and SOC2 report after the call.
[05:12] Maya: good. any detail on enrollment for canary/rollouts? we want auditability for model rollbacks.
[05:18] Samira: rollouts are versioned, and our console keeps an immutable rollout log. you can require approval gates for model promotions and we provide an audit trail for who rolled what and when.
[05:29] Dr. Park: last thing — retention windows. you mentioned export to S3; can you support multi-tier retention (90d hot, 1yr warm, 7yr cold archival)?
[05:38] Jules: yes — we can configure export lifecycles to a customer S3 bucket with lifecycle rules to Glacier or equivalent. for hosted customers we offer retention policies up to 1 year; longer archivals usually move to Dedicated/Private or customer-hosted storage.
[05:50] Maya: makes sense. also, encryption in transit — do you support mTLS for service-to-service inside Dedicated?
[05:58] Samira: yes, mTLS is supported for Dedicated and Private. hosted supports TLS; we can discuss dedicated peering and additional network-level controls in the SOW.
[06:09] Ravi: curious — competitors? are customers choosing Anthropic multitenant or building in-house?
[06:15] Evan: we've seen all three. Anthropic and Vertex are used by some for quick hosted use, while others combine Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and lower unit costs vs building in-house.
[06:27] Maya: can we get a sample audit export and a sample SCIM mapping example?
[06:31] Jules: yes, i'll drop both links. for now, quick pointers — link to security artifacts and pilot intake doc: https://redwood.example.com/security/ntq-2026 and pilot sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark-example (will share direct).
[06:48] Samira: ok, next steps recap in chat: we'll send the SOC2 and ISO artifacts, sample audit export, and SSO/SCIM guide. then schedule a pilot run in dedicated eu-west pool with your test dataset.
[06:57] Maya: sounds good. one last question — do you support token-level cost breaks by batching? we need to estimate monthly spend for 100k queries/day.
[07:05] Samira: yes — Optimize layer can suggest batching and prefix caching; for interactive workloads we estimate per-token cost with batch size 1, but caching and KV reuse can reduce cost significantly for repeated prompts. we'll run the numbers in the pilot.
[07:19] Evan: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot scheduling.
[07:26] Ravi: thanks — appreciate it.

Note: transcript includes occasional transcription artifacts and speaker overlaps; timestamps are approximate.

End of call.
